### introDuction **•** **_The mixed economic signals from the United States and China, along with the potential for escalation of the sovereign debt problems in Europe and uncertainty ahead of elections, all helped to keep investors largely risk-averse in April. There is little as yet to suggest that this situation will change much in May, although clearly the election results in Europe will shed some light on the likely path of European negotiations over the rest of this year. We expect precious metal prices to continue to drift lower in May, although it is possible that palladium may have already seen its low._** **•** **_Investors have been showing cautious signs of fresh interest in the market and the official sector has again attracted comments in the press as a buyer of gold. While dollar instruments remain in demand, however, and in the face of sluggish fundamentals, gold may dip below $1,600 in May before re-grouping and preparing for an assault on $1,900 before year-end in the face of sustained ultra-loose monetary policy and excessive government debt levels._** **•** **_Silver is gradually building support at $28-30 after a two-month slide from $38 in late February. Silver has been focusing on the uncertain economic outlook and investor longs on Comex have been heavily reduced while shorts have expanded. It could thus have periods of spiky action due to any short covering ac

tivity, but sentiment is very cautious and a dip below $29 is foreseeable in May before consolidation. Renewed strength towards $40 later in the year is likely to have to be led by gold._** **•** **_Platinum remained out of favour with investors during April, sliding to an intraday low of $1,533 under sustained liquidation and increased short selling on Nymex, plus light sales from ETFs. The market remains in a surplus and has to struggle with heavy inventory levels and we expect prices to_** **_continue to slip in May before the sector as a whole regains its poise. Platinum’s loose association with gold as a “precious” metal should help it to recover later in the year and a test of $1,775 is possible before year-end._** **•** **_Palladium, however, may have started to turn the corner already. Still in deficit (though also with high inventories), palladium sentiment is likely to be more responsive to any improvement in any of the major regional auto sectors. A challenge of $775 is likely before year-end. ##### The foMc; will they, won’t they? 

yet again the markets have continued to scrutinise any pronouncement from members of the federal open Market committee in an effort to peer into the future.  recent signals have been mixed; as described in the Gold chapter of this publication, there is now a range of views within the foMc as to the favoured time for the first hike in interest rates (three of the 17 Members recently polled were in favour of 2012), while on the other hand Dr. Bernanke has not yet ruled out a further round of easing. 

it is arguable that investors are fatigued to a degree with interpreting such statements, but the markets must, to a large extent, remain in thrall to the vicissitudes of economic forces.  in principle, north america looks as if it is withstanding the easterly winds blowing across the 

atlantic, but it still too soon to say that the economy can shrug off any further contagion from europe. 

Meanwhile the soaring cost of spanish debt, plus 25% local unemployment and a bursting property bubble has weighed heavily on sentiment towards europe.  spain is now in recession, while the German manufacturing sector shrank in april at the fastest pace in three years, raising doubts about Germany’s scope to continue to drive growth in the eurozone.  The German bond auction in mid-april was not fully covered, attracting bids of only Є2.4Bn against a target of Є3Bn.  This has attracted a mixed reaction; either that Germany was about to become tainted by contagion, or that it is now a

st to double its lending capacity (although the Bric nations did not contribute to any increase, in an effort to demonstrate frustration at the lack of re-weighting of voting power, better to reflect relative national economic power). The iMf stated that the funds would be drawn only if needed and, if drawn, would be refunded with interest. however, the programme has raised some criticism on speculation that eurozone members might _de facto_ have first call on any funds and that this would reduce any fiscal discipline. The european central Bank President has endorsed austerity programmes in the eu, while warning also about inflation. results of the french and Greek elections are likely to be the key elements that inform short-term market sentiment in May and could lead to commodity volatility. We believe though that the global view points to further downward drift before improvements in the second half of this year. **I3** May 2012 - IntroductIon confidential - not for distribution

_Continued uncertainty about the economic outlook resulted in reduced activity in the gold market in April and the price is likely to continue to drift until there is a clearer perception of the next overall direction. Gold’s range (simple ratio based on high/low) was just 3% during the start of April and early May, while silver, platinum and palladium all traded in a 7% range. Palladium’s favourable fundamentals meant that it staged a small gain over the period._ _From the start of May 2011 to early May 2012, gold remained the outperformer as an uncertain economic outlook kept the rest of the sector under pressure. Silver’s net change was minimal as it hovered between precious and industrial characteristics, while platinum suffered particularly from concerns about the European auto sector. Palladium’s weakness was exacerbated by profit taking (and probably also distress selling), notably from the ETF launched in January 2010._ ###### siGnificanT eQuiTy inDices, 2011 To aPril 2012 ###### euroPean cDs raTes* 125

### GOLD **•** **_The main feature in gold at present is how rangebound the market has become. Jewellery demand, and possibly also some official sector bargain hunting, are defending the downside, but there is little upward momentum and investors are taking some profits. Until there are clearer signs of an economic trend developing (in either direction), prices are likely to continue to drift._** **•** **_After opening at $1,664 in April and moving towards $1,680 at the start of the month, the FOMC minutes of the mid-March meeting forced prices rapidly down to $1,610, since when the trend has been broadly sideways._** **•** **_Sentiment was still cautious, however, as the signals from the US are mixed and the continued uncertainty about the Eurozone in particular, allied also to fluctuating signals from China, meant that investors spent much of April in “risk-off” mode and cash holdings are now approaching near three-year highs. In late April the open interest in Comex gold contracts was at its lowest since the start of September 2009, although there was a small increase towards month-end._** **•** **_Similarly the net investor long position on Comex was substantially below the twelve-month average, while activity in exchange traded instruments was limited._** **•** **_Official policy and pronouncements remained the keys to gold market sentiment in recent weeks. The Federal Reserve in the United States is of course a primary focus, with the Eurozone crisis simmering in the background and election campaigning in France and Greece also keeping the markets cautious about Europe. Industrial figures from China, and their implications for monetary policy, were important._** **•** **_The physical market improved during April as the Indian jewellers’ strike came to an end, and ahead of the important Akshaya Tritiya festival (24th April), but the Indian wedding season is now over and this is likely to undermine physical demand again. Rupee weakness has also started to deter interest to a degree. The Chinese market, while clearly still amenable to bargain hunting, is generally steady._** **•** **_The price traded between $1,610 and $1,6

80 during April, ending on a relatively upbeat note (closing at $1,651.25) as the markets read an increased possibility of QE3 into the FOMC late-April Statement. A number of news stories concerning fresh central bank gold purchases also helped to underpin sentiment._** The price outlook is essentially unchanged, with weakness likely in the near-term, but renewed strength in the second half, possibly accompanied by wide swings We continue to expect gold prices to drift lower in the short term, and it remains possible that prices may look below $1,600 during May. it is likely also that the dollar will remain robust against the euro in the coming months, especially if further downgrades mean that european institutions look to increase dollar-based positions in us instruments. We should not forget how institutions were lenders of gold in december in a rush to bolster their balance sheets with dollars ahead of the year-end. subsequent gold borrowing in January suggests tha

t these positions were at least partially unwound in January. While we are not necessarily forecasting that something similar could develop during June, the possibility should not be ruled out and this could help to keep gold under a degree of pressure during the rest of the second quarter.
